entries: Watch out: features are not grown by choice: the cactus in the hot, dry desert has a thick stem that stores water like a bottle, sharp thorns that stop thirsty animals biting it, and deep roots that find water - and none of these features was grown by choice.
slots.label: Not grown by choice
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Blending in keeps animals safe: the moth's wings are the same colour as the tree bark, so it blends into its home and hungry birds fly right past without seeing it.
slots.label: Blending in keeps animals safe
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Birds travel far to survive: when winter comes and food is hard to find, the birds fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places, then return when spring brings food back.
slots.label: Birds travel far to survive
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: People change animal homes: when people clear forests to build farms and roads, the trees go and the animals that lived there lose their food and shelter.
slots.label: People change animal homes
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A special feature of a living thing that helps it survive in its home: a thick stem, camouflage colours or a long migration journey.
slots.label: Adaptation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Blending in with your home: the moth's wings match the tree bark, so hungry birds cannot spot it.
slots.label: Camouflage
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The long yearly journey some birds make: flying thousands of kilometres to warmer places for winter and returning in spring.
slots.label: Migration
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The place where a living thing lives, which gives it food and shelter: a desert, a tree or a forest.
slots.label: Habitat
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: To stay alive in your home: a living thing survives when its features help it find food and water and stay safe.
slots.label: Survive
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The many groups of parents and young over a very long time: features develop slowly over many, many generations, not overnight.
slots.label: Generations
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
